 Live updates by Lucas Monteiro
 1:05 PM ET 21 minutes ago Speak, Des Buckingham! – Al-Kholood Head Coach
 I don’t want to be a coach who just tries not to lose games. We have a clear way of working—a brand and an identity built on ball possession. Traditionally, football has always been a sport where the coach is expected to shout from the touchline for 90 minutes straight, just to make it look like they know what they’re talking about. The game has changed. If we’ve done our work during the week, the players know the plan, and the match itself just comes down to a few timely reminders. There are teams here now with an attacking line that wouldn’t look out of place in the Premier League. We’ve achieved our primary objective—securing our spot in the Saudi Pro League for next season—while also making history by reaching the club’s first-ever King’s Cup final and qualifying for the Saudi Super Cup.
 Live updates by Lucas Monteiro
 12:44 PM ET 42 minutes ago Speak, Ange Postecoglou! – Al-Nassr Manager
 It’s not that I make a habit of winning trophies, but I always win something in my second year. Nothing has changed. I’ve said it before, I don’t say things unless I truly believe them. Get this into your heads: we never stop. We never stop. We only pause at halftime or after the match to celebrate. But during the game? We never stop. Throughout my entire career, people have told me that I only have a "Plan A"—and they’re right. My "Plan A" is to win things. That’s all I’ve ever tried to do in my career. We had 60,000 people in the stadium tonight, and I’m sure many of them walked in carrying problems from their own lives. For those 95 minutes, we helped them forget those troubles and feel good. That’s something special.
